"data": {"label": "Help"}, "elements": [{"node": "mhp_20", "element": "tab", "data": {"label": "Getting started"}, "elements": [{"node": "mhp_21", "element": "markdown", "data": {"label": "Getting started", "value": "## How it works

Loopar manages your clients' email through **Migadu** (the mailboxes) and **Cloudflare** (the DNS). Every change you make here is sent to them; you never need to open their panels for day-to-day work.

1. **Settings, once** — open [Mail Hosting Settings](</desk/Mail Hosting Settings/update>) and enter your Migadu admin email, a Migadu API key (*Migadu → My Account → API Keys*) and a Cloudflare API token with *Zone → DNS → Edit*.
2. **Add the client's domain** — [Mail Domain → New](</desk/Mail Domain/create>). Type the domain (e.g. `client.com`) and pick the customer. Saving creates it in Migadu, or adopts it if it already exists there. Domains you already had in Migadu come in with **Import from Migadu** on the list.
3. **DNS** — on the domain, **Preview DNS** shows what would change; **Configure DNS** writes the records in Cloudflare (MX, SPF, DKIM, DMARC and the verification record). An existing SPF is merged, never duplicated.
4. **Activate** — a few minutes later, **Check & activate**. The status turns **Active** when Migadu sees the records.
5. **Mailboxes** — create one per person ([Mailbox → New](</desk/Mailbox/create>)). See the *Give a client an email* tab.
6. **Aliases** — addresses that forward to mailboxes of the same domain, e.g. `sales@` → `ana@`, `luis@` ([Mail Alias](</desk/Mail Alias/list>)).

> The *DNS report* and *Migadu check* fields on each domain keep the result of the last run.
"}}]}, {"node": "mhp_22", "element": "tab", "data": {"label": "Give a client an email"}, "elements": [{"node": "mhp_23", "element": "markdown", "data": {"label": "Give a client an email", "value": "## Create the mailbox

1. [Mailbox → New](</desk/Mailbox/create>).
2. **User**: the part before the @ (`mercedes`). **Domain**: the client's domain. **Display name**: the name people see (`Mercedes López`).
3. **Invitation / recovery email**: the person's **personal** email (Gmail, iCloud…). It must be a different address than the new mailbox.
4. Save. Migadu emails that personal address a link to **choose the password**. Loopar never knows it.

## What the client does

1. Opens the invitation email from Migadu and sets the password.
2. Uses the mailbox in any of these ways:

| Where | How |
|---|---|
| Browser | **webmail.migadu.com** — user: the full address, the password they chose |
| iPhone / Mac Mail | *Add account → Other → Mail*. Usually the address and password are enough (auto-configuration) |
| Outlook / Android / others | IMAP **imap.migadu.com** port **993** (SSL) · SMTP **smtp.migadu.com** port **465** (SSL) · user: the full address |

## When something goes wrong

- **The invitation didn't arrive** — check the spam folder, then use **Send invitation** on the mailbox (you can change the address there).
- **They forgot the password** — **Send invitation** again; they choose a new one.
- **You need to set it yourself** — **Set password** (at least 10 characters). It goes to Migadu only; give it to the person through a safe channel.
- **A person leaves** — turn off *Can send* / *Can receive*, or delete the mailbox. **Deleting deletes the mail in Migadu.**
"}}]}, {"node": "mhp_24", "element": "tab", "data": {"label": "Mail apps"}, "elements": [{"node": "mhp_25", "element": "markdown", "data": {"label": "Mail apps", "value": "## Which app to use

Every app below works with Migadu (IMAP + SMTP). If the person already uses a mail app, add the new account there: it changes their routine the least.

| Device | Recommended | Alternative |
|---|---|---|
| **iPhone / iPad** | **Apple Mail** — built in, notifications, usually configures itself | Gmail or Outlook, if they already use them |
| **Android** | **Gmail app** — *Add account → Other (IMAP)* | **Thunderbird for Android**, free and connects directly |
| **Mac** | **Apple Mail** | Thunderbird |
| **Windows** | **Thunderbird** — free, connects directly to Migadu | Outlook, if the company already uses it |
| **No install** | **webmail.migadu.com** | — |

## Settings

| | Server | Port | Security |
|---|---|---|---|
| Incoming (IMAP) | imap.migadu.com | 993 | SSL/TLS |
| Outgoing (SMTP) | smtp.migadu.com | 465 (or 587) | SSL/TLS (or STARTTLS) |

User: the **full address** for both; same password.

## Good to know

- **Webmail** is enough for people who check mail now and then; it has no notifications and the session expires.
- **Outlook** (new desktop and mobile) syncs IMAP accounts through Microsoft's servers, which keep the password. For privacy-sensitive clients prefer Apple Mail or Thunderbird.
- Don't set up Gmail **web** to "check mail from other accounts" (POP): Google announced it is retiring it. The Gmail **app** with IMAP is different and keeps working.
"}}]}, {"node": "mhp_26", "element": "tab", "data": {"label": "DNS explained"}, "elements": [{"node": "mhp_27", "element": "markdown", "data": {"label": "DNS explained", "value": "## The records and why

| Record | What it does |
|---|---|
| **MX** `aspmx1/2.migadu.com` | Tells the world where to deliver the domain's mail. MX of other providers (e.g. Cloudflare Email Routing) are removed so mail isn't split. |
| **SPF** (TXT `v=spf1 …`) | Which servers may send as the domain. Only **one** SPF is allowed: an existing one is merged with `include:spf.migadu.com`. |
| **DKIM** (3 CNAME `key1..3._domainkey`) | Signs outgoing mail. They must be **DNS only** (grey cloud), never proxied. |
| **DMARC** (TXT `_dmarc`) | What receivers do with mail that fails SPF/DKIM. A valid existing policy is kept; an invalid one is replaced with the policy from the settings. |
| **Verification** (TXT `hosted-email-verify=…`) | Proves to Migadu the domain is yours. |

## Manual DNS

When a domain's DNS is not on Cloudflare (e.g. GoDaddy), set **DNS = Manual** on the domain, copy the records from Migadu's panel into that provider, then use **Check & activate**.

## Checking delivery

Send a message to a Gmail account and open *Show original*: **SPF**, **DKIM** and **DMARC** should say **PASS**.
"}}]}, {"node": "mhp_28", "element": "tab", "data": {"label": "Limits & tips"}, "elements": [{"node": "mhp_29", "element": "markdown", "data": {"label": "Limits & tips", "value": "## Your Migadu plan

- Sending and receiving limits are **per Migadu account**, shared by **all** your clients' domains. One client sending too much affects the others.
- Website notifications, contact forms and password emails from Loopar should go through a transactional service (SES, Resend, Postmark), not through these mailboxes.

## Good to know

- Migadu's API can't delete a domain: deleting a **Mail Domain** here only removes it from Loopar. Remove it in Migadu's panel.
- **Sync mailboxes** (on a domain) or **Import from Migadu** (on the list) bring changes made directly in Migadu into Loopar. Nothing is deleted by a sync.
- If Migadu fails while deleting a mailbox, the record is removed from Loopar and the mail stays untouched; a sync brings it back.
